Absence of gravitational polarization mechanism
in the canonical bimetric theoryPreprint: DESY-23-010

August 8, 2026
Abstract

Motivated by a version of the “Dipolar Dark Matter” model, that aims at a relativistic completion of the phenomenology of MOND, we investigate the gravitational polarization mechanism in the canonical bimetric theory with an effective matter coupling. We explicitly show the fundamental obstacle why such theories cannot achieve a consistent gravitational polarization, and thus fail to recover the MONDian phenomenology at low energies.

pacs
95.35.+d, 04.50.Kd

I Introduction

Despite passing all current tests with flying colors (the last in date being the discovery of gravitational waves Abbott et al. 2016; Abbott et al. 2017), our theory of General Relativity (GR) suffers from some “darkness”, i.e., yet ambiguous gravitational phenomena that can be explained either by invoking non-gravitational ingredients, or by “beyond-GR” completions Heisenberg 2019. The paramount instance is that stars orbiting in periphery of galaxies do not move accordingly to GR predictions Bosma 1981; Rubin et al. 1982, but instead behave as if the visible mass of the galaxy was only a small fraction of the total mass. The usual way to address this “missing mass” problem is to postulate the existence of some unknown non-relativistic form of matter, insensitive to electromagnetic forces (otherwise it would have already been seen), coined “cold dark matter” Bertone et al. 2005. If this paradigm is a cornerstone of current physics, there is still no evidence of this new particle, despite decades of experimental efforts Aprile et al. 2020; Albert et al. 2020; Aad et al. 2021.

Another way to explain the missing mass problem could be to consider that in some regime, the laws of gravity deviate from GR. This path has been initiated by the 40-years old seminal work of Milgrom Milgrom 1983, setting a very simple modification of Newton’s law that accounts for the motion of stars in galaxies and provides a natural explanation for the Tully-Fischer relation. Nevertheless, the MOND (for MOdified Newtonian Dynamics) approach is yet only phenomenological, despite great efforts to embed it within a viable fundamental theory (see e.g. Bekenstein 2004; Bruneton and Esposito-Farèse 2007; Deffayet et al. 2014, and Famaey and McGaugh 2012 for a comprehensive review on the MONDian approach). An alternative possibility to build such a relativistic completion is to exploit the dielectric analogy of MOND Blanchet 2007, which has led to several “Dipolar Dark Matter” (DDM) models Blanchet and Le Tiec 2008; Blanchet and Le Tiec 2009; Bernard and Blanchet 2015; Blanchet and Heisenberg 2015a; Blanchet and Heisenberg 2015b; Blanchet and Heisenberg 2017. In the present work, we focus on a subclass of such models Blanchet and Heisenberg 2015a; Blanchet and Heisenberg 2015b; Blanchet and Heisenberg 2017 that are based on a bimetric extension of GR in which the two metrics are supposed to host opposite “gravitational charges” (see also Milgrom 2009 for a different type of MONDian bimetric theory).

Thus the DDM phenomenology relies on a mechanism of gravitational polarization associated with opposite gravitational charges. It was indeed claimed in Blanchet and Heisenberg 2015b, that in the non-relativistic limit, using the canonical bimetric theory, the matter present in each sector feel forces with opposite signs, leading to the desired polarization. Nevertheless, as shown in the present work, due to a missing term in Blanchet and Heisenberg 2015b, unfortunately such polarisation mechanism cannot happen in this bimetric framework, which ruins this DDM model. However previously proposed DDM models Blanchet and Le Tiec 2008; Blanchet and Le Tiec 2009 in standard GR are still viable.

The plan of this paper is as follows. The DDM model used, which is an extension of the one studied in Blanchet and Heisenberg 2015b; Blanchet and Heisenberg 2017, is presented in Sec. II. The proof of the impossibility of a gravitational polarization mechanism in this general set up is then exposed in Sec. III. Concluding remarks are presented in Sec. IV.

II Model

Note that the interaction term (7) induces a supplementary, although indirect, coupling between the two metrics, and can thus reintroduce the ghost that was suppressed by the interaction term (3) de Rham et al. 2015; de Rham et al. 2014. Restricting the interaction term to the case αn=α4−n​βn\alpha_{n}=\alpha^{4-n}\beta^{n} as was done previously, it has been shown that the ghost is not excited for energies beyond the decoupling limit of the theory Blanchet and Heisenberg 2017. In our more general framework (3), it could be that the theory is plagued by a ghost at energies well below the decoupling limit. Nevertheless, as our aim is to prove that those theories are not well suited for a MONDian phenomenology, and as such a ghost would definitively not play a role in this low-energy analysis, we will consider the larger class of theories with (7) and arbitrary coefficients {αn}\{\alpha_{n}\}.

III Proof of the absence of polarization mechanism

Let us now turn to the study of the weak-field (non-relativistic) limit of the theory (1), investigated along the lines of Blanchet and Heisenberg 2015b. In order to reach a consistent weak-field limit, we assume that the Universe is empty in average, i.e. that the matter only enters at perturbative order in the action. Moreover, seeking for a viable gravitational polarization mechanism requires to perturb both metrics around a common background metric, say g¯μ​ν\bar{g}_{\mu\nu}. Note that, as we will see later on, an empty background is not necessarily a flat one, as the interaction term will play the role of an effective cosmological constant. Thus g¯μ​ν\bar{g}_{\mu\nu} is not the Minkowskian metric, but rather a de Sitter (or anti-de Sitter) one. We then perturb each metric as

gμ​ν\displaystyle g_{\mu\nu} =(g¯μ​ν+hμ​ν)2≡(g¯μ​ρ+hμ​ρ)​g¯ρ​λ​(g¯λ​ν+hλ​ν),\displaystyle=(\bar{g}_{\mu\nu}+h_{\mu\nu})^{2}\equiv(\bar{g}_{\mu\rho}+h_{\mu\rho})\bar{g}^{\rho\lambda}(\bar{g}_{\lambda\nu}+h_{\lambda\nu})\,, (8)
fμ​ν\displaystyle f_{\mu\nu} =(g¯μ​ν+ℓμ​ν)2≡(g¯μ​ρ+ℓμ​ρ)​g¯ρ​λ​(g¯λ​ν+ℓλ​ν).\displaystyle=(\bar{g}_{\mu\nu}+\ell_{\mu\nu})^{2}\equiv(\bar{g}_{\mu\rho}+\ell_{\mu\rho})\bar{g}^{\rho\lambda}(\bar{g}_{\lambda\nu}+\ell_{\lambda\nu})\,.

We now investigate the phenomenological consequences of this constraint in the non-relativistic limit c→∞c\to\infty. In this regime, we consider Newtonian-like systems, with sizes significantly smaller that the effects of a reasonable cosmological constant. We can thus discard the effect of the effective cosmological constant Λ\Lambda, and take a Minkowskian ansatz for g¯μ​ν\bar{g}_{\mu\nu}, which allows a proper 3+1 decomposition of the components. On this flat background, we parametrize the metric perturbations by single Newtonian potentials UgU_{g} and UfU_{f} and two “PPN” constants γg\gamma_{g} and γf\gamma_{f} as

h00=Ugc2+𝒪(1c4),h0​i=𝒪(1c3),hi​j=γgUgc2δi​j+𝒪(1c4),\displaystyle h^{00}=\frac{U_{g}}{c^{2}}+\mathcal{O}\left(\frac{1}{c^{4}}\right)\,,\qquad h^{0i}=\mathcal{O}\left(\frac{1}{c^{3}}\right)\,,\qquad h^{ij}=\gamma_{g}\,\frac{U_{g}}{c^{2}}\,\delta_{ij}+\mathcal{O}\left(\frac{1}{c^{4}}\right)\,, (21)

The i​jij components of the field equations (17) set γg=γf=1\gamma_{g}=\gamma_{f}=1, and the constraint equation (20) then gives

∂i[Ug−Uf]=0.\partial_{i}\big[U_{g}-U_{f}\big]=0\,. (22)

However, the gravitational polarization mechanism discussed in Blanchet and Heisenberg 2015b required that the gradients of UgU_{g} and UfU_{f} have opposite signs: as the particles described by JgμJ_{g}^{\mu} and JfμJ_{f}^{\mu} feel the force respectively due to the potentials UgU_{g} and UfU_{f}, they will be displaced in the opposite direction. The U⁡(1)U(1) field AμA_{\mu} coupling both sectors would then create an effective polarization of the spacetime medium, reproducing the main feature of the model Blanchet 2007. It is thus clear that the constraint (22) is incompatible with such a mechanism.

IV Conclusion

This study has proven that, contrarily to what was claimed in the work Blanchet and Heisenberg 2015b, the framework based on canonical bimetric theory is unable to produce a consistent gravitational polarization mechanism. This shortage unfortunately spoils its capacity to account for an effective MONDian phenomenology, and thus, to be a proper relativistic completion of the MOND paradigm. Note that another DDM model, based on standard GR Blanchet and Le Tiec 2008; Blanchet and Le Tiec 2009, is still viable in this respect; this model has recently been simulated numerically on galactic scales Stahl et al. 2022. Nevertheless, there is still hope that a viable mechanism could be achieved in a ghost-free bigravity framework, as DDM was based on the Hassan-Rosen model, but other bimetric theories exist, for instance the newly proposed minimal bigravity De Felice et al. 2021, which has the advantage of having stable cosmological solutions as well as escaping the Higuchi ghost present in usual bigravity scenarii.
